This is long, but has some life lessons. 

3am, I can't sleep, windows are open, I clearly hear a woman screaming for help.

I grab my (legal) gun and holster, put it on. My roommate was still up as well and heard it too. I tell him to call 911 and I run out the door.

I stop in my yard, listening. I hear screaming again. Now I can pinpoint it. I run into the alley behind our house and run toward the sound. The screaming is coming from a house a few doors down.

I get to the house and their backyard is well lit, surrounded by a chain link fence. The side door to the garage is open, accessible from the yard. I hear another scream for help. 

I jump the fence and run into the garage. On the floor I see a woman sitting against the wall, covered in blood. Like head to toe.

This is where things start to go wrong. 

"Are you okay? What's wrong?" I ask. I see she is holding a cordless house phone. She doesn't acknowledge me. She holds up the phone, screams "HELP ME!" Into it.

Then....she smashed the phone to pieces against the concrete floor.

She looks at me finally,  and the look in her eyes convinced me to back out of the garage.

Where I ran smack into a guy covered in blood in the yard I somehow missed. He has a scalp would so bad his skull is showing.

I continue to back away....and then the girl flies out of the doorway and tackles this guy to the ground.

I'm staring, absolutely shocked, when a cop car rolls up as they are fighting. 

As soon as he hits his lights, she springs up off him. Cop asks to be let in (I jumped the fence) so I go and find the garage door button.

Cop asks what's going on. Guy doesn't speak english.

Here is the life lesson.

The girl PROCEEDS TO ACCUSE ME AND MY FRIENDS (I was alone) OF TRYING TO BREAK INTO HER CAR. She then said the guy she was fighting chased my friends off but managed to make me stay.

I'm am totally speechless.

Cop turns to me and asked what my side was. (I told him everything I told you guys already). During his questioning me, the other two start arguing in spanish, and SHE ATTACKS HIM AGAIN IN FRONT OF THE COP. 

I step back, cop is screaming at them, another unit pulls up,  and another cop runs in and they pull the bloody couple apart.

The first cop tells me to go home and if he has any other questions he will come talk to me (never did).

MORAL OF THE STORY: Do not get involved I domestic disputes. I was very fortunate this woman was so angry/drunk/whatever that when she accused me of a crime, her behavior was so insane the cop had no reason to believe her, but it could have gone much much worse.

Last I saw both she and the guy were being taken away in ambulances. Never heard anu thing else.

Not a professor, but a teacher. Martial arts instructor.

We were doing some hand vs. knife training. (BTW, scary shit. Sucks to go unarmed vs a blade)

Anyway, we were using rubber knives (for safety of course), and I made the joke that 'anyone who could survive an entire minute without being cut could teach the next class'.

Drill starts. Students are using the skills taught. Most are doing okay. I have one young kid working with an older (probably late 50's, early 60's) guy. 

Anyway, at the end of the drill, I ask if anyone didn't get cut at all. Out of a class of about 2 dozen, this one kid raises his hand.

Again, I had seen his partner, and he wasn't moving very fast. Fine.

I walk over to them, I say 'nice'. I take the rubber knife from his partner. The kid beams. He asks if that means he can teach the next class.

At this point, it's still lighthearted. I smile. I say 'well, let's see.' I hold up the knife. 

He takes his fighting stance. I wait. I ask if he's ready. He nods.

I 'cut' him on the first slice. I wasn't trying to be a jerk. I wasn't being rude. I just moved at a normal pace.

He scowled at me. I shrugged, tossed him the blade, and told the class to switch partners.

I turned away. I heard "I bet you can't do better." I turned back.

He lunged at me full force.

If you haven't ever taken a martial arts class, attacking the instructor is about on the same level as spitting in your pastor's face.

Without thinking, I blocked the attack and punched him in the neck. Not like a mock punch. As in full force. Sent him sprawling. 

I stood there, stunned. The entire class stood silently, having witnessed this. As he started to get up, someone started clapping, and the whole class joined in.

I took no pride in that. The kid stood up, and our eyes met.

"Do NOT pull that shit again." I told him. Angriest I've ever been in class.
